chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
If a man cuts from his hair with his teeth, he should wipe it with water before he performs salat (prayer). He said: There is no harm; that only applies to iron.
His statement, 'That only applies to iron,' is to be understood as carrying a kind of recommendation, not obligation.
ai.seo_question: Does someone need to wash after cutting hair with the teeth before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on cutting hair with the teeth and whether washing afterward is required before salat (prayer). The text indicates there is no harm in it, and clarifies that concern specifically relates to iron, with the instruction understood as recommended rather than obligatory.
